regime.label: Short-gamma grind toward the 1080 call wall with IV compressing
evidence: Net dealer gamma only flips positive at 1080 (call OI 1,534) - spot at 1047.1 sits inside the short-gamma zone below that flip, so dealers are still trading with the tape below 1080.
The 1080 call wall has grown 42.7% in three sessions (1,076 -> 1,110 -> 1,534 OI), with 580 contracts of volume today confirming live, Vol2Vol-passing flow rather than stale OI.
ATM IV has compressed 15.3% in three sessions (17.35% -> 15.78% -> 14.71%) even as the future rallied 33.8 points (+3.3%) - a calm-grind pattern, not a panic squeeze.
25-delta skew is near-flat at +0.4 (put 15.74% vs call 15.35%), well below a typical protective put-rich index skew, showing call demand has caught up to puts as spot climbed.

S50U26.today_summary: S50U26 future settled 1047.1, up 16 points (+1.55%) today and +33.8 points (+3.3%) over the past three sessions. Max pain sits at 1030, 17.1 points below spot, while the 1080 call wall (OI 1,534, +38% today alone) is the nearest resistance and the near-money put support has migrated up to 1030 (OI 758). ATM IV is 14.71%, compressed 15.3% versus three sessions ago, implying a 1-sigma daily move of just 9.7 points. Dealer gamma turns positive only at 1080, so the whole 33-point stretch between spot and the wall remains short-gamma territory.
what_changed: Max pain drifted 20 points higher in three sessions (1010 -> 1020 -> 1030) but spot outran it, widening the spot-to-pain gap from 3.3 to 17.1 points.
Call wall OI at 1080 jumped 42.7% (1,076 -> 1,534) while staying the single largest strike in the book across all three sessions - a persistent, multi-day build.
ATM IV fell from 17.35% to 14.71% (-15.3%) as the future rallied +3.3%, compression-into-strength rather than the IV expansion textbook squeezes usually show.
P/C OI ratio eased from a 1.22 peak (Jun 30) to 1.11 today as call OI grew faster than put OI day-on-day.
S50U26.five_day_thesis: Over the last three recorded sessions the S50U26 future climbed from 1013.3 to 1047.1 (+33.8 pts, +3.3%) while max pain crept only from 1010 to 1030 (+20 pts), so spot has pulled 17.1 points clear of its magnet versus just 3.3 points three sessions ago - a mild max-pain lag, not yet a confirmed failure, since IV is compressing (17.35% -> 14.71%) rather than expanding to confirm a breakout. The 1080 call wall has held as the single dominant strike all three sessions with OI up 42.7% (1,076 -> 1,534), while the near-money put floor has migrated up in lockstep with spot (1000 -> 1030 -> 1030), both consistent with real, tracked flow rather than stale positioning. Dealer gamma stays net short below 1080 throughout the period (cumulative GEX only turns positive at the top strike), so further advance toward that wall keeps dealers hedging with the tape, not against it. Net: a slow, IV-compressing grind higher that has not yet forced the short-gamma acceleration a decisive break of 1080 would trigger.

strategies.name: Call debit spread 1050C / 1080C
strategies.rationale: Short gamma below the 1080 wall plus a compressed 14.71% IV favors buying, not selling, upside convexity into the level dealers are actively defending.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid (spread width 30 minus received value), capped regardless of outcome.
strategies.invalidation: A close back below the 1030 near-money put wall / max pain, marking the uptrend stalling before the 1080 test.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1030P / 990P (hedge)
strategies.rationale: With put OI still building alongside calls and IV cheap in absolute terms, a defined-risk put spread is a low-cost hedge against a pullback toward max pain (1030) or the deeper 910 structural floor in this still-young 90-DTE series.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid (spread width 40 minus received value).
strategies.invalidation: A sustained close above the 1080 call wall, which would confirm the squeeze scenario over the hedge scenario.

S50U26.prediction: Bias stays bullish-but-orderly while spot holds above the 1030 max pain, with 1080 the level to watch - a confirmed break there (ideally with IV expansion, not just OI build) would flip the current short-gamma grind into a genuine squeeze; a fall back below 1030 would argue the three-session rally is stalling into the pain magnet. With IV compressing rather than expanding, a slow grind looks more likely than a violent break over the next few sessions.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice. SET50 options are cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the dealer-hedging mechanics behind any pin or wall are structurally weaker than for single stocks that settle in shares; treat 1030 (max pain) and 1080 (call wall) as tendencies, not guarantees, especially with 90 days still ahead to expiry.
